text:
ellie: Heads-up — we're rolling a split of the Vault transit policy (separating wrap/unwrapping from admin privileges) across staging clusters tonight. This is to add least-priv for our KMS-backed secrets. Leaving here so infra + oncall see it.
priya: Thanks. Which services will be touched? any customer-facing risk?
ellie: Staging-only for the first rollout: image-builder, model-harness, telemetry-ingest. No prod changes yet. Plan: 1) apply new transit-policy-v2 to staging namespaces, 2) run canary decrypts, 3) monitor audit logs for permission failures, 4) promote.
jordan: pinging @jordan oncall to watch for decrypt failures during the window (20:00 UTC). If we see >= 5 failed unwraps in 2m we'll rollback.
jordan: oncall here — I'll put ephemeral alert rule on the AuditLog stream and standby. Slack alert + pager if threshold hit.
sam: Should we add a temporary fallback role that allows unwrap for specific service accounts during rollout? avoids broad admin grants.
ellie: yes — creating a fallback role bound to the three service accounts only. Fallback TTL 6hr. After canary we remove it.
ellie: quick commands I'm running:
```
# create new policy
vault policy write transit-wrap-v2 transit-wrap-v2.hcl
# bind to k8s service account (example)
vault write auth/kubernetes/role/image-builder-role bound_service_account_names=image-builder bound_service_account_namespaces=staging policies=transit-wrap-v2 ttl=24h
```
priya: How are we going to validate that KMS rewraps still function for longer-lived tokens? any automated test?
ellie: good call — I'll run a batch job that rewraps 200 test blobs using the same key and verify unwraps. Also will tail Vault audit logs for these patterns: "request":"transit/unwrap" and look for "permission denied" entries.
vault-bot: new audit sink connected to splunk-staging at 2026-03-23T19:42:10Z — forwarding events.
priya: Can you share the Splunk query you'll use? I'll add it to the runbook.
ellie: Splunk query (rough):
```
index=vault_logs source=transit action=unwrap | stats count by service_account, response_code | where response_code="403"
```
jordan: If the count spikes, are we going to auto-backout or manual? I prefer manual with 5m fast rollback window.
sam: Manual rollback is safer here. We should, however, enable a script to rebind old policy quickly. I'll prepare a one-liner.
ellie: prepared rollback snippet:
```
# rebind old policy to svcaccts
vault write auth/kubernetes/role/image-builder-role policies=transit-wrap-old
```
ellie: Also note we'll create an event in the security ticketing system and tag the audit artifacts: ticket SEC-9876. Leaving the ticket reference in case we need post-rollout trace.
priya: Sounds good. After rollout let's run an RBAC audit: compare principals with unwrap events and ensure no unexpected identities. I'll own that after rollout.
jordan: oncall will keep watches until +30m post promotion. If anything odd, page me immediately.
ellie: rolling at 20:00 UTC. I'll post a short status update in this thread at start, mid, and finish. :thumbsup:
ellie: 20:02 UTC — applied transit-wrap-v2 to staging-image-builder, canary unwraps succeeded (0 failures in 100 attempts).
ellie: 20:10 UTC — promoted to all staging namespaces. Monitoring audit logs.
ellie: 20:28 UTC — audit shows 2 permission-denied unwraps from telemetry-ingest SA, I just attached fallback role and re-ran unwraps, success now. Added note in SEC-9876.
priya: thanks — will run the RBAC comparison now and report anomalies in the ticket.
jordan: all quiet on the pager front. Leaving watch for 30m.
ellie: final: rollout looks clean. Removing fallback role and scheduling a 48h post-change audit. Closing the incident card in SEC-9876 and filing a short postmortem w/ recommendations: include automated pre-rollout unwrap test and pre-wired fallback role for future.
vault-bot: policy-change audit event recorded (actor=ellie, policy=transit-wrap-v2, change_id=zc-9a3b).
